monocarboxylateds are taken up by skeletal muscle mitochondria via the MCT1 and/or MCT4, and that MCT2 is associated with both SS- and IMF-mitochondria.
subsarcolemal (SS) and interfibrillar (IF) mitochondria have different distributions of the monocarboxylater transporters (MCTS).
subsarcolemnal and intermyofibillar mitochondria are different in their ability to oxidize monocarboxylated substrates.

the role of MCTs in the regulation of energy metabolism in the heart and skeletal muscle.
the role of MCTs in the regulation of energy metabolism.
the role of mitochondria in the regulation of cellular metabolism, with particular emphasis on the regulation of mitochondrial metabolism by the cytoplasmic metabolite, pyruvate.

MCT2 is present in both SS and IMF, whereas MCT1 and 4 are only present in SS mitochondria.
MCTs are present in SS mitochondria but are absent from IMF mitochondria.

MCT1 and 4 are located at the plasma membrane, and MCT1, and MCT2 are located in the subsarcolemal mitochondria.
